63-077.r: Tinkathia system (Champaran) → indigo on 3/20 of land; Raj Kumar Shukla drew Gandhi's attention to indigo peasants; Champaran = Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India.

63-084.r: 'Tinkathia' Kanoon → Champaran, Indigo (Neel); cultivators forced to grow indigo on 3/20th of holdings; Gandhi's first Satyagraha there in 1917.

63-085.r: Raj Kumar Shukla (not Rajendra Prasad) persuaded Gandhi to come to Champaran; colleagues: J.B. Kripalani, Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha, Mahadev Desai, Braj Kishor Prasad.
63-085.t: Rajendra Prasad joined at Champaran but did not invite Gandhi; Raj Kumar Shukla did.

63-088.r: Champaran movement was basically against (forced) cash crops.

63-089.r: Mahatma Gandhi opposed planned development, industrialisation and mechanisation; favoured cottage and village industries, labour-intensive work, Gram Swaraj.

63-090.r: Not connected with Champaran → Jai Prakash Narayan (also Ram Manohar Lohia); connected: Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha, J.B. Kripalani.

63-092.r: Significant aspect of Champaran Satyagraha (1917), per book → drastic decrease in cultivation of plantation and commercial crops.

63-093.r: Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee (by Government-Gandhi agreement) → President F.G. Slay; members incl. D.J. Reid, Mahatma Gandhi, L.C. Adami, Raja Harihar Prasad; Anugrah Narayan not a member.

63-095.r: British response to Champaran Movement (1917) → set up Champaran Agrarian Committee to look into peasants' grievances.

63-096.r: Gandhi's first successful Satyagraha after return (1915) → Champaran, Bihar, 1917, at Raj Kumar Shukla's request; also his first farmers' movement.

63-102.r: Raj Kumar Shukla, an indigo cultivator, invited Gandhi to Champaran; Gandhi arrived 10 April 1917 with Brajkishore, Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha, Kripalani.

63-103.r: Raj Kumar Shukla met Gandhi at Lucknow and requested him to visit Champaran.

63-104.r: Champaran Satyagraha was local (peasants, anti-Tinkathia; Rajendra Prasad, J.B. Kripalani helped), not all-India; Gandhi's first national-level movement → Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919).

63-105.r: National leader of Champaran Indigo movement → Mahatma Gandhi.

63-106.r: N.G. Ranga opposed Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha; Rabindranath Tagore gave Gandhi the title 'Mahatma' during it.

63-107.r: Kheda Satyagraha (Gujarat) → government did not suspend land revenue despite famine/drought (true); Permanent Settlement proposal for Gujarat is false.

64-001.r: First peasant movement of India → Bijolia (Mewar, Rajasthan); led by Sadhu Sitaram Das (1913), later Vijay Singh Pathik (1915).

64-002.r: Bijolia (Mewar, from 1897, about 44 years; Sadhu Sitaram Das, then Vijay Singh Pathik) → news carried by Prayag's Abhyudaya and Calcutta's Bharat Mitra; Pathik-Gandhi statement marked false.

64-003.r: U.P. Kisan Sabha (February 1918) → Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi (Home Rule activists), supported by Madan Mohan Malaviya; Jawaharlal Nehru not associated.

64-005.r: 'Nai-Dhobi Bandh' (social boycott, end of 1919) → started by farmers of an estate in Pratapgarh district; Baba Ramchandra organised farmers in Awadh.

64-007.r: Baba Ram Chandra → Sanyasi, ex-indentured labourer in Fiji, recited Tulsidas Ramayana; organised Oudh peasants against landlords during Non-Cooperation.

64-008.r: 1930s peasant movements: Sahajanand Saraswati → Bihar; Khudai Khidmatgars → NWFP; Swami Ramanand → Hyderabad; Abdul Hamid Khan → Southern Assam.

64-009.r: 1930s Kisan Sabha Movement → Swami Sahajanand; founded Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha; President of first All India Kisan Conference, Lucknow 1936.

64-010.r: Eka Movement (Oudh, end of 1921; Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur; Madari Pasi) → aim: convert rent into cash; issues: rents 50 per cent above record, Thikedar oppression.

64-012.r: Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha → Swami Sahajanand Saraswati; All India Kisan Congress (Lucknow, April 1936) → President Sahajanand, General Secretary N.G. Ranga.

64-013.r: Sahajanand Saraswati published newspaper 'Lok Sangraha' to highlight peasants' hardships.

64-014.r: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati (1889-1950), Sanyasi and Bihar peasant leader → ran Hindi weekly 'Hunkar' from Patna.
64-014.t: Sahajanand is linked to both 'Hunkar' (weekly, Patna) and 'Lok Sangraha'; check which one is in the options.

64-016.r: All India Kisan Congress (later All India Kisan Sabha) → Lucknow, April 1936; first President Swami Sahajanand Saraswati; General Secretary N.G. Ranga.

64-023.r: Bihar Kisan Sabha (1929) → Swami Sahajanand Saraswati; helped by Karyanand Sharma, Rahul Sankrityayan, Yadunandan Sharma, Panchanan Sharma → all connected.

64-024.r: Just before his death (1950), Sahajanand formed All India United Kisan Sabha → demand: nationalisation of land and waterways.

64-025.r: First All India Kisan Sabha meeting (Lucknow, April 1936) → presided by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati; addressed by Jawaharlal Nehru; N.G. Ranga secretary.

64-026.r: Kisan Movement in Bihar → Dr. Rajendra Prasad (later President of Constituent Assembly and first President of India).

64-027.r: Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; Bhartiya Kisan Vidyalaya → N.G. Ranga; Bengal Praja Party → Fazlul Haq; Bakasht Agitation → Swami Sahajanand Saraswati (list prints 'Shraddhananda').
64-027.c: The Bakasht agitation in Bihar was led by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati; the list and the book wrongly say Swami Shraddhananda. Code (b) still fits by elimination.

64-031.r: Gandhi gave Vallabhbhai Patel the title 'Sardar' (on behalf of Bardoli women) for leading the Bardoli Satyagraha.

64-033.r: Tebhaga Movement (Bengal, 1946, Bengal Provincial Kisan Sabha) → cut landlord's share from one-half to one-third of crop (Flood Commission); led to Bargadari Act.
64-033.h: Tebhaga = 'three shares' → landlord gets only one-third.

64-034.r: Tebhaga Movement 1946, Bengal → led by Kisan Sabha; demand: landlord's share cut from half to one-third of harvest.

64-035.r: Bhoodan Movement → Vinoba Bhave, 18 April 1951, Pochampalli, Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana); Jaya Prakash Narayan joined in 1954.

64-036.r: Bhoodan began at Pochampalli (18 April 1951): Zamindar Ramachandra Reddy donated 100 acres; landlords asked to gift at least one-sixth of land (Sarvodaya Samaj).

64-038.r: Bhoodan Movement → Vinoba Bhave (after Independence), to give land to landless farmers; he was first Individual Satyagrahi in 1940.

65-001.r: First modern trade union → Labour Union, 1918, by B.P. Wadia and V. Kalyanasundaram (textile workers of Buckingham and Carnatic Mills).

65-002.r: Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association → founded 25 February 1920 by Anasuya Sarabhai and Mahatma Gandhi, after Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918.

65-003.r: AITUC → founded at Bombay, 31 October 1920, by N.M. Joshi; first President Lala Lajpat Rai; Vice President Joseph Baptista; General Secretary Diwan Chaman Lal.
65-003.t: Founder N.M. Joshi, but first President Lala Lajpat Rai.

65-009.r: AITUC Nagpur session 1929 → presided by Jawaharlal Nehru; Left-Right clash; moderates N.M. Joshi, V.V. Giri, B. Shiva Rao broke away to a separate body.

65-010.r: AITUC founded 1920; first President Lala Lajpat Rai (both true); All India Trade Union Federation formed 1929 by Moderates under N.M. Joshi, not S.A. Dange (false).

65-011.r: First Indian member of Communist International (founded 1919 by Lenin) → M.N. Roy, who visited Moscow on Lenin's invitation.

65-012.r: Communist Party of India founded at Tashkent, 17 October 1920 → group headed by M.N. Roy (with Abani Mukherjee, M.P.T. Acharya and others).

65-013.r: Kanpur Conspiracy Case → against leaders of Communist Movement (M.N. Roy, Muzaffar Ahmed, S.A. Dange, Shauqat Usmani and others).

65-014.r: Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929-33): 32 labour leaders charged, incl. two Britishers → world-wide sympathy from Einstein, H.G. Wells, Harold Laski, Roosevelt.

65-015.r: Revolutionary (militant) phase of Indian trade union movement → 1926-1939; leaders M.N. Roy, Muzaffar Ahmed, S.A. Dange, Shauqat Usmani.

65-016.r: Radical Democratic Party (1940) → M.N. Roy; 'Bandi Jeevan' → written by Shachindranath Sanyal.

65-017.r: Revolutionary Communist Party of India (RCPI) → Saumyendranath Tagore, 1934, breaking away from CPI.
65-017.t: Don't confuse with M.N. Roy's Radical Democratic Party.

65-018.r: Workers and Peasants Party grew provincially: Labour Swaraj Party (Bengal 1925) → WPP Bengal 1926, Bombay 1927, U.P. 1928; aim: radicalise Congress from within (only 2 true).
